extra.message: User input from request.args.get('search') is concatenated directly into SQL string via f-string on line 137. The search_query is not sanitized or parameterized, allowing SQL injection attacks via the search parameter.

User-supplied picture_url from request body is passed directly to requests.get() without validation. This allows SSRF attacks where an attacker can scan internal networks, access cloud metadata services (e.g., http://169.254.169.254/), or probe internal endpoints.

The UserProfile GET endpoint has @token_required decorator commented out (lines 152-153), disabling authentication. Any unauthenticated user can retrieve any user's profile by providing their user_id in query parameters. This is CWE-862 (Missing Authorization).

The UserProfileUpdate POST endpoint has @token_required decorator commented out (lines 221-222), disabling authentication. Additionally, the authorization check at line 187 only verifies the user_id in JSON body matches session, but a malicious user can modify other users' roles/permissions if they can guess or obtain a user_id. No proper authorization check exists.

The UserDelete DELETE endpoint has @token_required decorator commented out (line 221-222) and no authorization check whatsoever. Any unauthenticated or authenticated user can delete any user account by providing their user_id. This is a Broken Function Level Authorization vulnerability (CWE-284/CWE-862).

The uploaded_file route receives a filename parameter that is passed directly to send_from_directory() without any sanitization. An attacker could use path traversal sequences like '../../../etc/passwd' to access files outside the uploads directory (CWE-22).

The download_file route receives a filename parameter that is passed directly to send_from_directory() without sanitization. Path traversal attacks are possible via filenames containing '../' sequences (CWE-22).
The delete_file route receives a filename parameter that is used to construct file_path and passed to os.remove() without sanitization. Path traversal attacks possible via '../' in filename (CWE-22).
The profile_pictures route has no authentication check at all. Anyone can access any profile picture without being logged in, potentially exposing user profile images.

Passwords are hashed using MD5 (custom_hash function on line 403). MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsuitable for password hashing. An attacker with database access can trivially reverse password hashes.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

DEBUG = True in production configuration allows detailed error messages and stack traces to be displayed to users, potentially exposing sensitive information (CWE-11).

extra.message: SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = False disables the HttpOnly flag on session cookies, allowing session tokens to be accessed via JavaScript. Combined with any XSS vulnerability, this enables session hijacking attacks.
The search route echoes user-provided query back in the results without escaping. If the template renders results without proper escaping, this enables reflected XSS attacks via the query parameter.
